definitions.note: to rook someone is to swindle them, here a verb

parts.note: something finished is over, done with
to charge is to rush at in attack

explanation.surface: A chess player, having lost the castle, sees the game end in a sudden assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like the chess piece; it is the verb meaning to cheat someone out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook a customer is to fleece them, charging far more than something is worth.

clue.text: Article in large house that adds taste

indicators.note: in places the article inside the word for the big house

parts.note: a villa is a large country house
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature on a stately home claims to lend it some refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is a flavouring added to food to give it a sweet taste.

indicators.note: abandoning says the hundred leaves the word for the boat

parts.note: a craft is a boat or ship
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A great many people, a hundred of them, desert a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is an informal phrase for a great many of them.

definitions.meaning: Jean ... was the 1930s Hollywood platinum-blonde film star
A new town in Essex, a county east of London

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Hollywood star is shared with a post-war new town in the county of Essex.

clue.text: Critic of satirical show heard by Queen

indicators.note: heard says the show's name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a revue is a stage show of sketches, often satirical
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's verdict on a satirical show is listened to by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer writes critical assessments of books, plays or films for publication.

clue.text: Provide witty remark after end of satire

indicators.note: after puts the remark behind the single letter
end of picks out the final letter of the word satire

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A comedian supplies a wisecrack at the close of a satirical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or supply them with what they need.

indicators.note: wearing means the friend has the relaxing word on, round its middle

parts.note: china, from rhyming slang china plate = mate, means friend; the 's is read as 'is'
to chill is to relax

explanation.surface: Someone lounges about in a borrowed fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for friend is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent, prized for coats.

clue.text: Exchange views about one pine, perhaps

indicators.note: about says the discussing word goes round the single letter

parts.note: to confer is to talk together and exchange views
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Two people discuss a single tree, or someone pining away.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is one example of a cone-bearing evergreen tree, hence the 'perhaps'.

parts.note: seals, as a verb, means shuts or closes
to have something is to experience it, as in having a good time

explanation.surface: Seals in the sea have a lucky escape from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' reads as the animals but is the verb meaning shuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an idiom for a near miss, a danger only just avoided.

clue.text: Guarantee cry of pain after volts applied

indicators.note: after puts the cry of pain behind the electrical symbol

parts.note: V is the symbol for volts
ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: A shriek of pain is certain once a current is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch for something is to give a personal assurance that it is true or good.

clue.text: Just on left, close to lay-by

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of lay-by

explanation.surface: Driving directions: carry on, keep left, until near the roadside stopping place.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British term for a roadside parking area.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and this word are synonyms in the sense of merely, as in 'just a minute'.

parts.note: homes are dwellings
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: Plain houses are mocked with a bit of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, from cloth woven at home.

definitions.meaning: shy describes someone bashful and reserved
turning in for the night, a sense of the verb retire

explanation.definitionFit: A bashful person is described as unassertive this way, and one who retires is turning in for the night.

clue.text: Nail polish back in style, man explains

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man explains a new style of manicure.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters LEMANE, read across 'style, man explains', are turned round by 'back'; the hiding itself goes unsignalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail varnish is commonly called enamel, a glossy hard coating.

clue.text: Lack of soil on ground, ultimately

indicators.note: on places the soil after that letter in the across entry
ultimately means the final letter of ground

parts.note: earth is soil

explanation.surface: A gardener complains of too little soil on the plot in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or shortage of something.

clue.text: Way to go about home system

indicators.note: about says the word for a path wraps around the at-home word

parts.note: a route is a way to go
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone explains a method of getting about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, regular procedure, a system for doing something.

clue.text: Mimic a bishop on board vessel

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so the bishop goes into the container

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop on a ship does impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a pot; 'on board' puts A and RR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or imitate without understanding, as the bird does.

indicators.note: replaced says the letters of the preceding words are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A wry remark about where many hip replacements are done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' does double duty: hip replacement surgery, and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip replacement operations are carried out in large numbers in medical wards.

definitions.meaning: to give up a plan or discard something
a brawl or scuffle, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: To ditch a plan is to drop it, and a scuffle is informally a scrap.

definitions.meaning: the male of the whale, like elephants and cattle, has this name

explanation.definitionFit: Male whales share the name of the male of cattle, and claptrap is called this informally.

indicators.note: Half means only the first four of the eight letters are used

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked

explanation.surface: A famous person poses partly undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for stark naked; its first half gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, a celebrity.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A know-all who writes music.
explanation.walkthrough: A clever dick is a British phrase for a smart alec.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La Traviata.

indicators.note: exotic suggests something foreign and strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone samples a foreign wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Compelling work, foremost of paintings by mature English artist

indicators.note: foremost of picks the first letter of paintings

parts.note: to age is to mature
J M W Turner was the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: An art book praising an elderly English painter's best pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping book that keeps the reader eager to continue is called this.
